comments.author: @tysoncung
comments.text: The part that surprised me most: the Nordic Language Convention has been in force since 1 March 1987, covering Danish, Norwegian, Swedish, Finnish and Icelandic across tax offices, schools, police, courts and health care, and outside criminal and court matters it largely reads as a recommendation. You have to ask for it, and plenty of officials have never heard of it. Sources are linked in the description. If you live in the Nordics, have you ever tried using your own language with an office abroad, and did it work?
